thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — sudden spike in 429/503 from hosted-api-us-east-1. 5m error rate > 8% for text-generation route. Automations: paging on-call. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/alerts/1748001234 :rotating_light:

mariam: I'm on it. Looking at the 1m/5m spike. Can someone grab tracing?

devon: grabbing traces now. Initial look: a small number of heavy customers are sending large concurrent streaming connections + long-running tokens. Appears to be queuing pressure on the routing layer.

mariam: ok. Plan: 1) apply temporary stricter rate limit at ingress (global per-IP and per-api-key), 2) disable streaming for non-enterprise tier (to reduce open connections), 3) throttle model concurrency from 256 -> 160 per-instance for the next 30m, 4) watch 429/503 graphs. Thoughts?

alex: +1 for disabling streaming for free tier. Can we do a soft quota bump for a handful of paying customers if they call CS?

jordan: I can triage customer-facing impact and notify top 10 tenants if needed. Which customers are affected?

devon: running query now — top offenders by requests in last 10min: cust-acme, cust-zenpay, cust-hypersvc. cust-acme is 40% of the surge.

mariam: I'll push ingress rule change. Command to update global rate limit: 

```
# curl to admin control plane
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://control.redwood/v1/rate-limits \
  -d '{"scope":"global","rules":[{"type":"api_key","limit_per_min":1200},{"type":"ip","limit_per_min":600}]}'
```

mariam: Applying now.

sre-bot: rate-limit update accepted (change-id: rl_20250722_01). Propagating to edge nodes.

devon: I also pushed a streaming flag toggle for plan!=enterprise: 

```
PATCH /config/feature_flags
{ "streaming_enabled_for_non_enterprise": false }
```

oncall-bot: feature flag change scheduled and rolled out in 45s.

mariam: throttling model concurrency on inference pool for text-gen-v2: 

```
POST /infra/pools/text-gen-v2/scale
{ "concurrency_per_instance": 160 }
```

mariam: Done. Watching dashboards.

incident-bot: Dashboard snapshot — 5m 429 rate down from 8.2% -> 4.5% in 10m. 503s unchanged at ~1.1% (some infra retries). Link: https://dash.redwood/internal/graphs/1748001234/snapshot

devon: good signal. We should also add a quick quota override for cust-acme and cust-zenpay via temporary bump so CS can approve and avoid churn. Suggest: cust-acme -> api-key-specific burst + allowlist for streaming (if they request emergency).

jordan: I'm reaching out to cust-acme now (DM sent). They report they launched a big batch job accidentally. They're happy to coordinate with rate limit exception for next 30m while they throttle their job.

mariam: I'll create a targeted exception: api-key exception with strict rate cap and shorter burst window. Command: 

```
POST /control/exceptions
{ "api_key": "cust-acme-key", "limits": {"per_min": 4000, "burst": 100}, "expires_in": 1800 }
```

mariam: Exception live for cust-acme.

incident-bot: Noted customer exception. Added to incident timeline.

devon: 429s continue to trend down, reaching 2.1% after 25m. 503s briefly spiked to 2.5% during concurrency change, likely due to some workers refusing new sessions, but auto-recovering. Logs show transient model warmup timeouts on a subset of instances.

mariam: rolled back the concurrency change slightly on smaller pool nodes (set 200 on n1-small) to reduce 503s. Command executed.

sre-bot: 503s dropping — now 0.6%. Overall request success > 99%.

alex: product question — did we have to disable any customer-visible features besides streaming? Will any customers see changed outputs?

devon: only non-enterprise streaming was disabled and some auto-scaling headroom adjustments. We'll surface in CS notes. No prompt-level changes.

jordan: told cust-acme and top-10 about mitigation steps and ETA for monitoring. They appreciated the exception.

mariam: summary timeline to capture in the incident:
- 0m: alert fired for elevated 429/503 (automated).
- 2m: on-call paged, initial triage.
- 6m: ingress global rate-limits tightened.
- 8m: streaming disabled for non-enterprise.
- 12m: model concurrency adjusted (160) -> caused brief 503 spike.
- 18m: per-customer exception created for cust-acme.
- 30m: metrics stabilized (429s -> 2%, 503s < 1%).

mariam: next steps: monitor for 60m, follow up with infra to investigate root cause (too many long-running streaming connections + bursty batch jobs). I'll create an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime and infra for postmortem.

devon: adding runbook link and suggested mitigations to incident ticket: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/live-mitigations.md

jordan: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note and CS follow-up.

alex: schedule a brief retro with product and infra tomorrow. Also check if rate-limiter thresholds should be adjusted by default per plan.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and in mitigation. Please add postmortem checkboxes when created.

mariam: marking thread resolved for active mitigation — metrics stable. Will update postmortem with exact root cause and fix plan. :white_check_mark:

devon: leaving a note: consider finer-grained streaming quotas by model + prioritized connection pool for enterprise customers to avoid broad feature-rollbacks next time.

sre-bot: Incident closed from "mitigation" state at 1748003840. Follow-ups: PROVIDE_POSTMORTEM (owner: mariam), ADJUST_RATE_LIMITS (owner: devon), CUSTOMER_COMM (owner: jordan).
